terms.comment: Classically comma (Greek κόμμα) is not the mark but the short phrase it divides off, which Cicero calls incīsum in Latin (Or. 211; Quint. 1.8.6, Lewis & Short); the name passed to the sign later.

sources: Lewis & Short: comma · Lewis & Short: incido
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 245.
